title: Go SDK: envelope-wrangler + typed-iterator pattern for streaming structured output
creator: Avery Martin
description: Introduce a composable 'envelope-wrangler' abstraction and a typed iterator pattern to make decoding, validation, incremental consumption, and deterministic retries of streaming structured outputs ergonomic in the Go SDK. The feature targets token/chunk streaming responses that emit a sequence of envelope frames (metadata, partial objects, diagnostics) and aims to provide: (1) a safe typed iterator over validated domain structs, (2) clear retry semantics when streaming fails mid-object, and (3) backpressure-friendly integration with existing client code and context cancellation.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a new EnvelopeWrangler type with a stable API that can accept raw stream frames and emit typed objects using generics (EnvelopeWrangler[T]).

Expose an Iterator API (Next() (T, error)) that returns a typed, fully-validated object or a terminal error; Next() must be safe to call from a single goroutine and should unblock quickly on context cancellation.

Add configurable retry policy hooks: onPartialObjectRetry, onTransientErr, and onFatalErr; default policy retries only idempotent stream restarts and replays prefixes when server supports resumable streams.

Examples demonstrating common patterns: decoding structured chat messages, embedding-stream envelopes, and function-call fragments with early validation and schema errors surfaced as domain-level errors.
Benchmarks showing decoder overhead < 8% at 32 concurrent streams for median 16-token objects compared to baseline untyped streaming decode.
Unit tests covering envelope validation, retry paths, cancellation, and backpressure interactions.
Docs + small snippet in README and Go SDK examples folder showing migration from raw stream handling to EnvelopeWrangler.
No breaking changes to existing streaming APIs; new types are additive.
design_notes: Problem: teams repeatedly implement ad-hoc streaming decoders that don't handle partial-object retries or consistent schema validation, causing silent contract drift and complex error handling.

Approach: centralize framing + validation logic in an EnvelopeWrangler that understands common envelope shapes (meta, delta, completion, diagnostic). Use Go generics for typed decode targets so the compiler helps callers work with typed domain objects.
Backpressure: iterator will expose a small internal buffer and allow callers to control prefetch via WithPrefetch(n). Prefetch default = 1 to keep latency low.

Retry model: two-layer strategy — fast local retry for transient transport errors (exponential backoff with jitter) and protocol-aware resume when server emits resume tokens. For non-resumable streams, Surface error and allow caller to re-request with idempotency token.

Validation: pluggable validators per type T; default validator performs JSON schema checks (if provided) and minimal semantic checks (required fields). Validation errors are returned by Next() as ValidationError with details.
Edge cases: mid-object EOF must be classified as partial-object and routed to onPartialObjectRetry; binary blobs are passed through as-is and not validated by JSON schema by default.
Compatibility: keep existing Stream->Decode primitive; EnvelopeWrangler wraps it. Non-streaming endpoints unaffected.
Telemetry: emit events for parse errors, retries, and validation failures to console and optionally to the Console via SDK instrumentation hooks.
Alternatives considered: codegen per-model decoders vs. runtime generic decoders. Chosen generics approach reduces codegen maintenance while giving type-safety for callers.
Open question: expose synchronous vs. asynchronous iterator variants? Start with synchronous Next() and evaluate async channel-based API in follow-up.
Performance constraints: must avoid reflection-heavy paths on happy path; use encoding/json with custom UnmarshalJSON on generated models where needed.
API sketch: type EnvelopeWrangler[T any] struct { FromStream(io.Reader) ... } func (w *EnvelopeWrangler[T]) Next(ctx context.Context) (T, error)
implementation_plan: Spike (2 days): implement minimal EnvelopeWrangler for sample model (ChatDelta) and measure overhead.
Core (3 days): implement generic wrapper, Next() API, validators, and basic retry hooks.
Integration (2 days): add examples for chat streaming and embedding-scoring stream, update README, and add migration guide.
Tests (2 days): property tests for partial frames, mock server tests for resume token behavior, unit tests for validators and retry hooks.
Benchmark (1 day): microbenchmarks comparing baseline stream decode vs EnvelopeWrangler for common object sizes and concurrency.
Docs + Release (1 day): write doc page, example PR, and changelog entry for sdk-go-0.26.
Implementation notes: avoid exposing internal frames type in public API; use functional options for configuration (WithRetryPolicy, WithValidator, WithPrefetch).
testing_plan: Unit tests for Next() happy path returning typed object for several model shapes.
Simulated partial-object streams that cut mid_json token to assert retry path is invoked and caller-visible error is correct.
Mock server tests for resume-token path: server provides resume token; test re-request and prefix replay behavior.
Load test: 1000 sequential Next() calls across 32 goroutines to validate buffer behavior and ensure no goroutine leaks.
Fuzz tests: random envelope mangling to ensure decoder doesn't panic and returns well-formed errors.
Benchmark: measure allocations and throughput at various prefetch settings.
Integration tests in CI that run with recorded gzipped streaming fixtures to avoid network flakiness.
E2E example: small sample app that streams chat messages, validates function-call fragments, and recovers from transient network error using the retry policy.
Test acceptance criteria: regression < 1% of previous CI coverage gaps and all new tests pass in under 4 minutes in CI.
Manual QA checklist: exercise cancellation, slow-consumer backpressure, and validation error visibility in logs.
rollout_plan: Opt-in alpha behind WithEnvelopeWrangler() factory; default SDK behavior unchanged.
Ship alpha in sdk-go-0.26-beta.1 and run dogfood tests with Platform Infra and one pilot customer team.
Collect telemetry and adjust prefetch defaults based on percentiles of Next() latency from dogfood runs.
Promote to GA in sdk-go-0.26 once benchmarks and dogfood feedback are green.
Deprecation path: after GA, publish migration examples and recommend EnvelopeWrangler for new streaming integrations.
Post-release: monitor for increased validation error rates and retry storms; add circuit-breaker heuristics if needed.
Support: include snippet in SDK changelog and sample migration PR template for customers.
Rollback: revert to previous non-wrangling decode path if critical regressions detected in first 72 hours post-release.
Telemetry gating: require <5% increase in p50 token latency for dogfood teams before GA.
Legal/Compliance: no PII surfaced by default; validators run locally; nothing is sent to telemetry unless explicitly enabled by WithTelemetryHook().
